headline: I study what happens where two materials meet.
definition: Ice on road surfaces, bitumen on stone, salt in freezing water. I model these interfaces molecule by molecule and test the models against experiments.
mission: I study what happens where two materials meet: ice on surfaces, bitumen on stone and salt in freezing water.

projects.title: Passive anti icing through surface design
projects.summary: I led a three-student team in laboratory research on superhydrophobic pavement coatings, studying water repellency, icing and mechanical performance.
projects.finding: The coating delayed droplet icing and reduced ice adhesion under the reported test conditions.
projects.purpose: Reduce reliance on energy intensive ice removal through passive surface design.

projects.title: Vibration controlled ice nucleation
projects.summary: I used molecular dynamics to investigate how surface vibrations promote or suppress ice nucleation in different water environments.
projects.finding: Confined water and interfacial nanofilms respond differently; vibration can favour nucleation or suppress it depending on geometry and conditions.
projects.purpose: Develop molecular guidance for efficient freezing and anti icing strategies.

projects.title: Chemical treatment of pavement interfaces
projects.summary: I contributed to experimental studies of silane coupling agents and lignin based polyurethane modifiers for asphalt adhesion.
projects.finding: These studies investigated improved adhesion and resistance to moisture or UV ageing using different chemical treatments.
projects.purpose: Support durable pavement materials with less maintenance and reconstruction.

projects.title: Molecular analysis of adhesive and cohesive failure
projects.summary: I modelled failure within bitumen and along bitumen mineral interfaces to connect molecular behaviour with observed debonding patterns.
projects.finding: The balance of adhesive and cohesive failure depends on material and loading conditions.
projects.purpose: Explain failure mechanisms that matter for pavement durability.

projects.title: Multiscale prediction of pull off strength
projects.summary: I linked molecular debonding behaviour to pull off experiments and strength prediction through multiscale modelling.
projects.finding: Simulation and experiment informed a modified strength model for bitumen aggregate interfaces.
projects.purpose: Provide engineering guidance for the design of more durable pavement materials.

projects.title: Molecular mechanisms for freeze desalination
projects.summary: I extended vibration controlled freezing research to saline water, studying the molecular processes relevant to freeze desalination.
projects.finding: The work connects interfacial ice nucleation and saltwater behaviour to questions of practical ice formation and separation.
projects.purpose: Contribute to more energy efficient routes to clean water.
projects.role: Researcher and named ARCHER2 case study author

projects.title: Ice nucleation at lipid bilayers
projects.summary: In an international collaboration with the University of Basel, I built a reproducible all-atom workflow to study how ice forms where water meets a lipid bilayer, using a software platform and a class of materials that were new to me.
projects.finding: I delivered a reproducible all-atom lipid–water simulation workflow within the collaboration.
projects.purpose: Extend ice-nucleation understanding from hard surfaces to soft, biological interfaces.

projects.title: Machine-learned force fields for water
projects.display_title: Sharper models for water and ice
projects.summary: Simple water models such as mW miss hydrogen-bond dynamics, which matter most at interfaces. I built a Python workflow to prepare and quality-check atomistic water data, then trained MACE neural-network potentials and compared them with simple baselines.
projects.finding: I set up a reproducible pipeline from raw atomistic data to trained and validated machine-learned water potentials.
projects.purpose: Make simulations of ice and saltwater more trustworthy for clean-water applications.
